title: pkg install <tool>@<version> ignores the version when the tool is already declared
description: Expected: asking for a version other than the declared one either installs or switches to it, or fails saying the tool is declared at a different version. Actual: pkg answers that the declared version is already installed, exits 0 and changes nothing, so the request is silently dropped. Repro on mise 2026.11.9 with pkg built from main (9d8bea6), where the global config declares node = "lts" and ripgrep = "latest": 'pkg install node@20 --dry-run' prints 'node 26.13.1 is already installed, declared in ...'; 'pkg install ripgrep@14.0.0 --dry-run' prints 'ripgrep 15.2.0 is already installed, ...'; 'pkg install xcode@16.4 --dry-run' prints 'xcode 27.2 is already installed, ...'. Suspected cause: crates/pkg-core/src/install.rs chooses Step::Unchanged from machine.declared_in(package) and States::installed, which both match on package.key and never compare package.version. Found while grounding proposal 0004 (Xcode management, PR #4). Out of scope there: 0004 gives xcode its own versioned operations and routes only xcode through them; every other tool keeps one declaration per name, and what a version request for an already declared tool should do is a separate decision.
